Trestle Freight would like to move this toward a written offer. My initial proposal is:

- **Role:** Mara would own the internal security platform, including its roadmap, identity-modernization integration, operating controls, and July audit-readiness deliverables.
- **Base salary:** **$182,000**.
- **Signing bonus:** **$18,000**, contingent on a mutually agreed start date at least six weeks before the July audit. If Mara needs a later start, I would propose a **$10,000** signing bonus and a revised readiness plan.
- **Initial site schedule:** For the first 12 weeks, Mara may choose either weekly site visits or **two three-day visits per month**, with reasonable travel expenses covered. The ongoing schedule can then be set around platform and team needs.
- **Incident coverage:** Business-hours coverage for Mara, provided she trains the designated escalation partner and supplies operating runbooks before handoff. The partner would handle after-hours escalation; this is not intended to create a routine 24/7 on-call obligation for Mara.
- **Audit plan:** Agree on concrete readiness milestones at the outset so platform ownership and audit expectations are unambiguous.

The key questions are Mara’s earliest practical start date and which site-visit structure she prefers. If those can be settled, I can incorporate any compensation adjustments into a complete written package.

Mara can start **June 1** with the **$18,000 signing bonus** confirmed in writing. She prefers **two three-day site visits per month**. I’d recommend the following package to her once we confirm the audit timing and staffing.

- **Compensation.** We propose **$195,000 base** for the architecture, operating controls, and audit responsibilities. Please confirm the audit date, whether June 1 qualifies for the $18,000 bonus, when it would be paid, and any repayment terms. If June 1 misses the six-week cutoff, we could still consider that date with a guaranteed **$12,000 make-whole payment**. Otherwise, Mara can start **July 1** with the proposed **$10,000 signing bonus** and a revised audit plan.
- **Architecture ownership.** The offer should give Mara decision authority over the internal security platform’s architecture and roadmap, including identity integration and operating controls. Please identify the executive who can resolve resource conflicts and approve risk exceptions.
- **Site visits.** We propose keeping the two grouped visits per month as the ongoing schedule, with reasonable travel expenses covered and any change by mutual agreement. The 12-week review can address which days on site are most valuable. Weekly commuting isn’t workable for Mara.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara can own business-hours response, train the escalation partner, and deliver the runbooks. Who will cover after hours from her first day, including during training and when the partner is unavailable? The written plan should assign primary and backup coverage so Mara never becomes the sole after-hours responder.
- **Audit readiness.** We propose an initial gap assessment, followed by a remediation plan with named owners and an evidence review before the audit. Please share the current readiness status and identify who owns work due before Mara starts. With that baseline and the audit date, we can agree on milestones she can reasonably own under either start date.

Trestle can confirm **June 1** and the full **$18,000 signing bonus**. Audit fieldwork is scheduled to begin **July 20**, so June 1 satisfies the early-start condition.

On compensation, Trestle can increase its proposal to **$190,000 base**, which is the most it can include in this package. Together with the June 1 start and full signing bonus, this provides **$208,000 in first-year cash compensation**, excluding benefits and covered travel. The bonus would be paid with Mara’s first regular payroll. It would be repayable on a prorated monthly basis only if Mara voluntarily resigns or is terminated for cause within 12 months; no repayment would apply following termination without cause.

The remaining terms can be documented as follows:

- **Architecture authority:** Mara will have decision authority over the platform’s architecture, roadmap, identity integration, and operating controls within the approved budget and security policies. The **Chief Information Officer** will serve as executive sponsor, resolve cross-functional resource conflicts, and approve any material budget changes or platform risk exceptions following security review.
- **Site schedule:** Two grouped, three-day site visits per month—six on-site days monthly—with reasonable travel expenses covered. This schedule applies during the initial 12 weeks and continues thereafter. The 12-week review may adjust which days are most valuable; any change to visit frequency or duration requires mutual agreement. Weekly commuting will not be required.
- **Incident coverage:** Mara owns business-hours response. From her first day until handoff, the existing security operations provider will be primary after hours, with the infrastructure operations on-call lead as backup. After Mara trains the designated escalation partner and delivers the runbooks, that partner becomes primary and the security operations provider remains backup. Training and initial runbooks will be completed within Mara’s first 30 days. Mara will not be the sole after-hours responder or acquire routine on-call duties without a separate written agreement.
- **Current audit baseline:** Core identity workflows are documented, but platform-control evidence remains incomplete and some remediation items still need named owners. The **security compliance manager** owns pre-start preparation and auditor coordination, including assembling the existing control inventory, prior evidence, open findings, and auditor requests before June 1.
- **Readiness milestones:** Mara will deliver the initial gap assessment by **June 12** and a remediation plan with named owners and dates by **June 19**. She will own platform work within her authority, while other control owners remain responsible for their assigned remediation. Mara and the compliance manager will conduct an evidence review by **July 6**, followed by a final readiness and open-exception review with the CIO by **July 13**. Mara is accountable for these deliverables, not for guaranteeing remediation by other teams or the audit outcome.

If Mara accepts the **$190,000 base** on this basis, Trestle can put this complete package into writing and recommend it.

The **$190,000 base** works for Mara as part of the complete June 1 package. I’m ready to recommend it to her. Please issue the written offer with the **$18,000 signing bonus** payable on her first regular payroll, the stated prorated repayment terms, and the architecture authority, travel schedule, incident coverage, and audit milestones in your proposal.

Please carry two operational dependencies into the offer. The June 12 gap assessment relies on the compliance manager assembling the audit materials before June 1. The after-hours handoff relies on the designated partner completing training and receiving the runbooks. If that takes longer than 30 days, the existing provider and infrastructure on-call lead should continue covering after hours until handoff.

Mara can make her final acceptance decision once she reviews the written offer.

## Trestle Freight — Written Offer Terms

Trestle Freight offers Mara ownership of its internal security platform on the following terms:

### Start date and compensation
- **Start date:** June 1.
- **Base salary:** **$190,000 annually**, paid through Trestle’s regular payroll.
- **Signing bonus:** **$18,000**, payable with Mara’s first regular payroll, subject to applicable withholdings.
- **Bonus repayment:** If Mara voluntarily resigns or is terminated for cause within her first 12 months, she will repay the bonus on a prorated monthly basis based on the uncompleted portion of that period. No repayment is required if Mara is terminated without cause.

### Platform ownership and authority
Mara will own the internal security platform, including its architecture, roadmap, identity-modernization integration, operating controls, and July audit-readiness deliverables.

Mara will have decision authority over these areas within the approved budget and security policies. The **Chief Information Officer** will serve as executive sponsor, resolve cross-functional resource conflicts, and approve material budget changes or platform risk exceptions following security review.

### Site visits and travel
- Mara will make **two grouped, three-day site visits per month**, totaling six on-site days monthly, with reasonable travel expenses covered.
- This schedule applies during the initial 12 weeks and continues thereafter. Weekly commuting is not required.
- The 12-week review may address which on-site days are most valuable. Any change to visit frequency or duration requires mutual agreement.

### Incident coverage
- Mara will own **business-hours incident response**.
- From her first day, the existing security operations provider will be the primary after-hours responder, with the infrastructure operations on-call lead as backup.
- Mara will train the designated escalation partner and deliver initial operating runbooks, targeting completion within her first 30 days.
- Handoff depends on the designated partner completing that training and receiving the runbooks. After handoff, the partner becomes primary after hours and the security operations provider remains backup.
- If handoff takes longer than 30 days, the existing provider and infrastructure on-call lead will continue their coverage until handoff is complete.
- Mara will not become the sole after-hours responder or assume routine on-call duties without a separate written agreement.

### July audit readiness
Audit fieldwork is scheduled to begin **July 20**.

The security compliance manager owns pre-start preparation and auditor coordination. Before June 1, that manager will assemble the existing control inventory, prior evidence, open findings, and auditor requests.

Agreed milestones are:
- **June 12:** Mara delivers the initial gap assessment.
- **June 19:** Mara delivers a remediation plan with named owners and completion dates.
- **July 6:** Mara and the compliance manager complete an evidence review.
- **July 13:** Mara, the compliance manager, and the CIO complete a final readiness and open-exception review.

The June 12 assessment expressly depends on the compliance manager assembling the audit materials before June 1. If those materials are delayed, the affected milestone dates will be promptly revised in writing with Mara.

Mara will own platform work within her authority; other control owners remain responsible for their assigned remediation. Mara is accountable for the deliverables above but does not guarantee remediation by other teams or the audit outcome.

I recommend that Mara accept the written offer as presented. It covers the cost of a June 1 start, gives her platform architecture authority, and keeps travel to two grouped visits per month. It also resolves both outstanding dependencies: after-hours coverage continues through handoff, and Mara and Trestle will revise affected audit dates in writing if the pre-start materials arrive late. Final acceptance rests with Mara.
